solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 3 down, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Surprising statement from lie-abed repulses Argie sportsman

indicators.note: to repulse is to drive back, so the statement is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a late sleeper who is out of bed early might surprise everyone with 'I am up!', giving AM UP

explanation.surface: A sporting Argentinian is put off by something a habitual sleeper-in says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argie' is British slang for an Argentinian; the Pumas are Argentina's national rugby union side, so one player is a Puma.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina's rugby team is nicknamed the Pumas, so each of its players is one of them.

clue.text: Stall for more incomprehensible dramatic work?

definitions.meaning: to feign reluctance so as to be pursued harder or offered more
a theatre piece that is difficult to understand: a play tough to grasp

explanation.surface: A theatregoer delays leaving in hope of more of an obscure drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning indifference to win more attention or a better offer; and literally a stage drama difficult to understand.

clue.text: Tom, Dick and Harry seducing Parisian husband with love song

indicators.note: seducing means taking in, so everyone wraps around the husband

parts.note: every Tom, Dick and Harry means everybody, so all
mari is French for husband
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Three ordinary men lure a Frenchman's spouse with a romantic ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Is This the Way to Amarillo' is a 1971 pop song by Tony Christie, named after a Texas city.

clue.text: Cast needs actor of an inferior quality

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould afresh, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre company's casting director grumbles that a performer just isn't good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' poses as the theatre's company of players, but it is the signal to rearrange 'needs actor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre or below par is described with this hyphenated adjective meaning not first class.

clue.text: Winter incurs it for dormice, as did the Bristol fire for Mr Park

definitions.meaning: dormice hibernate, sleeping through the cold months with bodily functions slowed almost to a stop

definitions.text: as did the Bristol fire for Mr Park
definitions.meaning: a 2005 fire at the Bristol warehouse of Nick Park's Aardman studio destroyed models and halted its stop-motion work

explanation.surface: Hibernating rodents and a studio blaze that hit the creator of Wallace and Gromit.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Park makes the Wallace and Gromit films at Aardman in Bristol; its archive store burned down in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernation is a near-halt of life functions, and a halted film studio has its cartoons on hold.

clue.text: Old actor kicking out on dancefloor, suppressing giggle

indicators.note: suppressing means holding in, so the dance encloses the giggle

parts.note: the Charleston is a 1920s dance known for its kicking steps
a giggle is a laugh

explanation.surface: A veteran performer dances wildly while trying not to giggle.
explanation.definitionFit: The English-born film star of the 1930s to 1960s played Henry VIII and Quasimodo.

clue.text: Lassie's outstanding heavenly body? Watch paparazzo do this!

definitions.meaning: the collie from the films was a canine celebrity
Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky
a photographer tailing a celebrity is said to dog a star

explanation.surface: A famous film collie is admired as a stunning sight, and the photographers follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie was a canine celebrity; Sirius is so named; and a paparazzo hounds celebrities.

clue.text: Slim-bodied fish-eater aroused by a second lover

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: aroused means raised up, and in a down entry that turns the word upwards

parts.note: the otter is a sleek river mammal that eats fish

explanation.surface: A lithe angler is stirred up by a second romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a little cupid, an embodiment of love, and so a lover.

clue.text: I0Us? Don't believe 'em!

definitions.meaning: I O U notes written with a zero instead of O, so pledges with nothing inside
pledges not worth trusting, which are hollow

explanation.surface: Warning against trusting IOU notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 0 in 'I0Us' is a zero, not a letter O: these debt notes are hollow, worth nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollow pledges that will not be honoured; an IOU is a pledge to pay.

clue.text: Rome reportedly the ultimate destination of these until time immemorial

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so what follows is a phrase heard spoken rather than a spelling

parts.note: the proverb says all roads lead to Rome, so Rome is where all ways end up

explanation.surface: A traveller's remark that Rome is where these routes finally end up, as they have done for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the saying 'all roads lead to Rome': the routes in question are 'all ways', which, said out loud, is a word for forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions describe something lasting forever or for as long as anyone can remember.

clue.text: Misguidedly go with Prague cohort

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the letters of the two words are set in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly travels to the Czech capital with a gang of companions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort in statistics is a band of people born around the same time, i.e. sharing a range of years.

clue.text: The driving force in healthy compound

indicators.note: in tells us the driving force sits inside the word for healthy

parts.note: hale means robustly healthy, as in hale and hearty
in Freud's theory the id is the instinctive drive within the mind

explanation.surface: A slogan claiming a motivating power lies within some health-giving mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A halide is a chemical compound of a halogen such as chlorine with another element, so it is a type of compound.

clue.text: Tough article secured by wit to bow of yacht

indicators.note: being secured by something means being held inside it

parts.note: Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, was a celebrated wit
the definite article is 'the'

indicators.note: the bow is the front end of a boat, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor's piece of gear is fastened by a clever person to the front of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat described as tough is chewy and hide-like, which is just what this adjective says.

clue.text: Perhaps middle-of-the-road poetry cheers guide

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the phrase is to be taken in a playful sense, here as sitting between two letters

parts.note: something middle-of-the-road sits between left and right, the letters L and R
odes are lyric poems, so poetry
ta is informal British for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Bland, unadventurous verse and toasts serve as someone's guiding light.
explanation.walkthrough: Politically, middle-of-the-road means neither left nor right: so the poetry and cheers are placed between L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used in navigation, hence figuratively any guiding principle.

clue.text: See 3
The old bird functions

definitions.meaning: an extinct flightless bird of Mauritius, the classic example of something long gone
a function is a party or 'do', so two of them make the answer

explanation.surface: An elderly woman still works perfectly well.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct Mauritian bird is the classic gone-for-good creature; and two parties, two 'dos', make up the word.

clue.text: Opening may hinge on this or get stuck in point of origin

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the point of origin

parts.note: DOB is date of birth, the point at which a life begins
taken as written
to jam is to stick fast

explanation.surface: A door either swings on this or gets wedged where it started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hinge on' looks like 'depend on' but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright side of a door frame is where hinges are fixed, so a door swings from it.

clue.text: Stroke made by Oxbridge printing house?

parts.note: Oxbridge is Oxford and Cambridge together, so a joint production is a co- one
UP is the abbreviation for University Press, as in OUP and CUP

explanation.surface: A literary triumph published jointly by Oxford and Cambridge's presses.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford and Cambridge each have a University Press (OUP and CUP); a book they put out together would be a co-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden successful move, a master stroke.

clue.text: Virgil's regular focus, support and protection for plant

definitions.meaning: in The Great Escape, Virgil Hilts, the Cooler King, kept throwing his baseball against the side of his prison room
the rigid outer layer of a plant cell, made of cellulose

explanation.surface: A Roman poet's habitual subject, and how to support and shield a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgil' suggests the Roman poet, but it is Steve McQueen's character in the war film The Great Escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilts bounced his ball off the side of his solitary-confinement room; plant cells have a rigid outer layer.

clue.text: See 7
Aim for perfection that is repressing energy in surrealist paintings

indicators.note: repressing means holding down within, so the outer piece encloses what follows

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: in puts the energy symbol inside the paintings

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a surrealist, so his paintings are Dalis
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Striving for flawless art means stifling the vigour found in surrealist canvases.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to picture something as perfect, aiming at a flawless version of it.

clue.text: Bill's ready to speak — or sing

definitions.meaning: a bill is a list of charges for goods or services
a singer in good voice is said to be '...', ready to perform

explanation.surface: A man called Bill is warmed up for a talk or a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill for goods supplied is the same thing as a trade invoice; split in two, the word reads as being in good vocal form.

clue.text: Full-bodied Bordeaux, say, swells uneasy girth

indicators.note: the wine goes inside and bulges out the waistline, so it is contained within
being uneasy means unsettled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Bordeaux is an example of French wine, vin

explanation.surface: Drinking rich claret makes an uncomfortable waistline grow larger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasy' rearranges GIRTH into THRIG, which the wine then bulges out from inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flourishing and full-bodied is in robust good health, growing vigorously.

clue.text: See 1 down
Out rating weaver

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
a loom is the machine that weaves cloth

explanation.surface: A deliberately terse phrase suggesting someone who weaves cloth has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out have opened, so the plant is in blossom.

clue.text: Cube, gift-wrapped? This may be steep

indicators.note: wrapped means enclosed, so the gift goes around the cube

parts.note: a grant is a sum given, a gift of money
a die is a small cube used in games

explanation.surface: Someone puzzles over a box-shaped present and whether its price is too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like a comment on cost, but it describes a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the slope of a hill or road, and slopes can be steep or gentle.

clue.text: Mythological soldier? Toughie solver might interpret it thus

definitions.text: Mythological soldier? Toughie solver might interpret it thus

parts.words: Mythological soldier? Toughie solver might interpret it thus
parts.note: split as sol-dier, a soldier becomes one who dies through the sun, the fate of the boy whose wax wings melted

explanation.surface: A seasoned puzzler explains how they would read a fighter from legend.
explanation.walkthrough: SOL is Latin for sun; a 'sol-dier' is one who died of the sun, as the winged youth of Greek myth did when he flew too high.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the son of Daedalus flew too near the sun on waxen wings and fell to his death.

clue.text: Inevitable recipient of lentil and bean casserole?

definitions.text: Inevitable recipient of lentil and bean casserole?

indicators.note: to casserole is to stew things together, so the letters of the two foods are mixed up

explanation.surface: Whatever lands on the cloth when a messy pulse stew is served.
explanation.definitionFit: The tablecloth and napkins are bound to catch spills from a sloppy stew.

clue.text: Shall we? Oh, yes — they lead to reserves

definitions.meaning: a suggestion to do something together, as in 'let us'
in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is played again, a re-serve

explanation.surface: An eager yes to a proposal, followed by a remark about what brings in substitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserves' looks like substitute players, but read it as re-serves: a let in tennis means the point is served again.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction proposes a shared action; in tennis lets are faults at the net that require a serve to be retaken.
